name: Parkes-Weber syndrome
aliases: capillary malformation with arteriovenous fistula and limb overgrowth

reference.source: ISSVA classification / Mulliken and Young's Vascular Anomalies
clinicalPearls: A high-flow overgrowth syndrome characterised by a cutaneous capillary malformation over a limb combined with multiple arteriovenous fistulae and diffuse limb hypertrophy
It is a fast-flow condition, which fundamentally distinguishes it from the slow-flow Klippel-Trenaunay syndrome despite superficial resemblance
Many cases fall within the RASA1-related spectrum of capillary malformation-AVM syndrome
A palpable thrill, audible bruit and warmth over the affected limb point to significant arteriovenous shunting
High-output cardiac failure can develop when shunting is extensive, particularly in infancy
Chronic shunting causes venous hypertension, skin changes, ulceration and limb-length discrepancy
Doppler ultrasound and MRA are central to confirming fast flow and mapping the fistulae
Management is multidisciplinary, involving compression, orthopaedic care of leg-length discrepancy, and selective embolisation of symptomatic fistulae
reference.pathophysiology: Parkes-Weber syndrome is a congenital fast-flow vascular anomaly in which a limb bears a capillary malformation together with numerous microscopic and macroscopic arteriovenous fistulae, causing direct arterial-to-venous shunting throughout the affected extremity. Many patients carry germline RASA1 variants within the capillary malformation-AVM spectrum, disrupting RAS-MAPK control of vascular differentiation. The persistent high-flow shunting drives limb overgrowth, venous hypertension and, when substantial, high-output cardiac strain; this fast-flow physiology is the key contrast with the slow-flow Klippel-Trenaunay syndrome.
additionalDifferentials: Klippel-Trenaunay syndrome (slow-flow, no significant AV shunting)
Isolated arteriovenous malformation of a limb
CLOVES and other PIK3CA-related overgrowth syndromes
Hereditary haemorrhagic telangiectasia with limb fistulae
additionalInvestigations: Doppler ultrasound to demonstrate fast flow and arteriovenous shunting
MRI/MRA to map fistulae, soft-tissue and bony overgrowth
Echocardiography to assess for high-output cardiac effects
Serial limb-length measurement and orthopaedic assessment
Catheter angiography when embolisation is planned
redFlags: Rapidly progressive limb enlargement or worsening pain
Non-healing ulceration or significant bleeding from the limb
Distal ischaemia or steal phenomena from shunting
New neurological symptoms if associated central nervous system lesions are present
reference.prognosis: Prognosis depends on the extent of arteriovenous shunting; limited disease may be managed conservatively, but extensive fistulae can cause progressive limb morbidity, ulceration and cardiac strain. High-flow lesions are difficult to cure and often require staged, palliative interventions with long-term follow-up.
pitfalls: Confusing it with slow-flow Klippel-Trenaunay syndrome and missing the high-flow shunting
Overlooking high-output cardiac effects in an infant with extensive fistulae
Attempting complete surgical cure of diffuse fistulae rather than selective control
Neglecting orthopaedic management of limb-length discrepancy
references: Mulliken and Young's Vascular Anomalies: Haemangiomas and Malformations
management: Manage the arteriovenous fistulae with staged catheter embolisation, reserving surgical resection for selected lesions, as high-flow disease is difficult to cure
Use compression garments and diligent skin and wound care to manage venous hypertension, oedema and ulceration
Treat high-output cardiac failure medically and by reducing the shunt burden, particularly in infancy
Address limb-length discrepancy and soft-tissue overgrowth with orthopaedic input, including shoe raises and timed epiphysiodesis
Consider targeted MEK-pathway inhibition such as trametinib for extensive RASA1-related disease within specialist or trial settings
Offer RASA1 genetic testing and family counselling given the capillary malformation-arteriovenous malformation spectrum
Monitor with serial echocardiography and limb imaging, coordinating care through a vascular anomalies multidisciplinary team
